claim: how large is the closed-loop PLL's own self-generated disturbance, in lock, on its shared VDD rail and on its VCO control node VCTRL -- the transient VDD/VCTRL ripple-in-lock measurement spec/decision-records/DR-006-statistical-rows-ratification.md names as the second prerequisite for row 13 Budget 1 (AC supply-ripple limit), and that design/loop-filter/DESIGN.md's row-13 headroom section names as owed. The DUT is design/top/top.sch (VCO + PFD/charge pump + loop filter + divider), driven from the same DR-005 cold start as sim/pll-lock (10 MHz reference, N = 25, 250 MHz target) through a 1 ohm resistive power-delivery stand-in between an ideal source and the block's VDD pin, and each point reports v(VDD) and v(VCTRL) peak-to-peak over the final 5 us of a 100 us transient, labelled with whether the loop was already in lock when that window began, across the DR-003 PVT grid (tt/ff/ss/sf/fs x -40/27/125 degC x 1.62/1.80/1.98 V).
spec_rows_note: spec/target-spec.md row 13 (supply sensitivity), which DR-006 leaves DRAFT -- this campaign is the evidence DR-006's 'What would ratify row 13' item 1 names for Budget 1 (the block's own rail disturbance, which decides whether a shared-rail ripple limit is a self-consistent contract at all), not a verdict on the row. Lock status and time-to-lock are also reported per point, but only as the context that decides whether a ripple window is in lock; sim/pll-lock is the campaign that cites row 8.
methodology_note: DUT and cold start are sim/pll-lock's, unchanged: design/top/top.sch strapped N = 25 against a 10 MHz reference, the same power-on RESETB pwl, and the same four DR-005 `measure.ic` cards (ring0 nudge per DR-004; VCTRL, CP and the loop filter's C1 internal node z1 forced discharged -- see spec/decision-records/DR-005-pll-lock-cold-start-initial-conditions.md), the same 100 us window, 172800 s per-point hang guard and sliding-window lock criterion as sim/pll-lock/testbench/tb.json, so this campaign's lock column is directly comparable to that campaign's. `require_lock` is false, per sim/pll-lock's own precedent: a point that never locks is recorded as evidence, not a harness failure. **Supply model (the one testbench difference, and the assumption every VDD number here rests on)**: an ideal source feeding the DUT's VDD directly makes v(VDD) ripple identically zero, so it cannot measure a self-generated rail disturbance at all. tb_loop_ripple.sch instead puts a 1 ohm series resistor (RPDN) between the ideal source (node VSUP, which the harness's supply_pattern patches per point) and the block's VDD pin, with no decoupling capacitance. That makes v(VDD) = V_supply - 1 ohm x I_VDD(t): the VDD ripple figure is numerically the block's own supply-current peak-to-peak in amperes times 1 ohm, and for a different purely resistive PDN it scales linearly with R. It is a conservative stand-in (no on-chip or package decoupling, which a real rail would have and which would attenuate the fast switching content), not a model of any particular package or power grid; the DC drop across RPDN is expected to be millivolt-scale at a milliampere-scale block current -- an expectation, not a measurement; each record's v(VDD) min..max column shows the actual rail level, against row 1's +/-10 % window. **Window**: ripple is the peak-to-peak over the FINAL 5 us of the transient (95-100 us, 50 reference periods), anchored to the end of the run rather than to the lock instant, because the lock criterion is a +/-5 % frequency band and a loop that has just entered it is still settling VCTRL -- a window starting at lock would fold that settling drift into the ripple figure. A window is labelled in lock only if the lock criterion was already met at 95 us. **Bandwidth**: the ripple nodes are `linearize`d onto the 20 ps transient grid before reduction, so excursions narrower than 20 ps are attenuated by the resampling; the VDD figure is the rail disturbance at that grid's bandwidth (up to 25 GHz), which is far wider than DR-006's 100 kHz - 100 MHz Budget 1 band, so it bounds the in-band content from above rather than measuring it. VCTRL sits behind the loop filter's R3/C3 pole, so its sub-20 ps content is expected (not shown) to be negligible. The grid was 200 ps until issue #210's ngspice-tolerance audit; it is now 20 ps, with the integration's own step cap held at 200 ps by `measure.tran_max_step` -- see the simulator-accuracy paragraph below. Both figures bound the in-band content from above, so the change does not invalidate the reading; it makes the bound looser and the peak-to-peak larger, because a finer grid attenuates less of the ring's per-edge crowbar content. A reader comparing a future record against any earlier informal 200 ps probe must therefore not read the difference as a change in the circuit. **Simulator accuracy** (issue #210, the ngspice-tolerance audit; the two knobs themselves are PR #209 / issue #202). This manifest runs under `.options reltol=1e-4` with a 20 ps dump grid and ngspice's internal timestep cap (the `tran` card's TMAX, `measure.tran_max_step`) pinned at the 200 ps this campaign was originally written against -- so the grid the ripple and edge times are read off is ten times finer than the cap the integration runs under, rather than equal to it. At ngspice's default reltol of 1e-3 the timestep controller's own local-truncation error is not a small perturbation on this DUT but a first-order effect: sim/integrator-floor measured 1.543 % RMS apparent period jitter on this design's own ring at a 200 ps grid for a DUT whose true period jitter is zero by construction, and misplaced that ring's frequency by ~2.9 % (243.8 against 251.1 MHz) -- records 20260925-201301-d8b1ab7.md (variant D) versus 20260925-203420-d8b1ab7.md (variant G). On the closed loop, those same defaults are what made sim/pll-lock-mc's first record report 3 locked draws all missing ratified row 9 (1.584 / 1.851 / 3.073 %) where the identical five seeds at reltol=1e-4 and a 20 ps grid report 5 locked draws all meeting it (0.554-0.717 %). A campaign whose entire output is the SIZE of a small self-generated disturbance cannot be run at a tolerance that manufactures disturbance of its own. The decoupled grid costs no integration -- measured on this design's ring, 109,986 internal steps at `tran 20p 6u 0 200p` against 109,989 at `tran 200p 6u` (sim/harness/measure.py) -- only a larger, uncommitted dump. The settings triple is the one sim/pll-lock, sim/pll-lock-mc, sim/lf-c1-jitter-sensitivity and sim/lf-c2-jitter-sensitivity all run this identical four-block DUT under, which is also what keeps this manifest's lock column comparable to sim/pll-lock's (an invariant sim/tests/test_harness.py pins); `timeout_s` rises from 43200 to 172800 to match them. **Cost**: this is sim/pll-lock's DUT and window, so it inherits that campaign's per-point cost (issue #103: ~6.8 wall-clock hours per point at 8 concurrent points on the reference host; see DR-004's status notes), and the tighter tolerance adds to it -- a record here may legitimately be a documented `--subset-reason` subset, and a point that times out is not evidence and must not be presented as one.
analysis: cold-start transient, closed loop (`tran 20p 100u 0 200p` preceded by `.options reltol=1e-4`, injected by sim/harness/measure.py from this manifest's own measure block -- see sim/loop-ripple/testbench/tb_loop_ripple.sch's header comment for why the schematic itself carries no .tran card), with v(CLK), v(VDD) and v(xxxtop.vctrl) linearized onto the 20 ps grid and dumped on one time column
